name: Strata Deep TunnelHide Mining Pressure Suit
description:
A hard-use tunneling and deep-mining suit designed for the pressurized subterranean extraction zones beneath M88. Outer shell is abrasion-resistant cordura-steel weave in matte charcoal, reinforced with ABS polymer impact panels at knees, elbows, and shoulders — panels are frequently cracked and field-replaced with scrap. A built-in exoframe harness runs along the spine and hips, providing load-bearing support for heavy equipment carry without a separate exoskeleton purchase.

The suit's hood integrates a sealed face shield with dust filtration and low-light optical enhancement. Collar carries a pressure equalization valve for rapid descent environments. Most miners mark their suits with paint or carved notches — personal identification in low-light tunnels where faces are hidden.
functionality: Impact and abrasion protection for tunnel environments. Spine-hip exoframe offloads up to 40kg of carried equipment weight. Pressure equalization valve rated for rapid descent to 400m. Low-light optical enhancement integrated into face shield. Spinal channel accommodates aug spinal rigs. Reinforced knee panels extend to digitigrade leg configurations.
what_it_says: You go underground and you come back up — you've made peace with the difference between those two things.
worn_by: Shelf tunnel-market operators who need protection
manufacturer: Strata Deep Industrial (Tier 2 corponation); knockoff panels from Shelf fabricators
story_hooks: A miner's suit has 47 carved notches on the left forearm — one for each shift at a depth that officially doesn't exist on any city map.
A tunnel collapse survivor was found three weeks later, suit still sealed — the pressure valve had kept them alive in a pocket, but the company had already filed the death paperwork.
Someone is running a side business selling 'certified' Strata Deep suits with forged inspection stamps; the exoframe harness bolts are the wrong alloy and will shear under load.

physical_description.visual_profile: A utilitarian, heavily armored one-piece suit that reads as industrial and brutalist. The silhouette is blocky and functional—broad shoulders from reinforcement panels, tapered slightly at the waist where the exoframe harness cinches, flared at hips for equipment attachment points. When worn, it dominates the wearer's form, making them appear larger and more geometric. The integrated hood and face shield give an insectoid, depersonalized appearance.
physical_description.fit: Compression-tight through the torso and limbs to accommodate the internal exoframe harness and pressure sealing. The reinforced panels sit proud of the base material, creating a segmented, articulated look. Glove cuffs and ankle seals are snug and lockable. Overall a technical, ergonomic fit designed for function over comfort.
physical_description.primary_material: Cordura-steel weave outer shell (charcoal matte), ABS polymer impact panels (knees, elbows, shoulders), silicone-sealed pressure bladder layer beneath, reinforced nylon webbing for harness integration
physical_description.texture: The main shell is smooth but slightly matte from abrasion and dust accumulation; scuffed in high-contact areas. The ABS panels have a harder, plasticky texture with visible stress cracks and stress-whitening. Where panels have been field-replaced with knock-off Shelf fab units, the mismatched texture is obvious—slightly shinier or rougher depending on source material. Welded seams are visible as raised ribbing.
physical_description.color_scheme: Matte charcoal-gray base with blackened ABS polymer panels. Accent colors are purely utilitarian: high-visibility yellow/orange striping on collar and wrists for rescue visibility; raw metal or dull copper at pressure valve and connector points. Hand-painted miner's marks (names, dates, tally notches) in white or bright spray paint vary by suit.
physical_description.closures: Heavy-duty friction-fit pressure seals at wrists and ankles; magnetic snap collar to secure hood; full-length dorsal spine zip (sealed and reinforced) running from neck to tailbone for entry/exit. Pressure equalization valve at collar is manual twist-lock design.
distinctive_features: Integrated exoframe harness running spine and hips—visible as reinforced webbing and attachment D-rings
Sealed face shield with dust filter cartridge (replaceable, often stained or clouded)
Low-light optical enhancement module on left temple (small raised housing)
Pressure equalization valve at collar—distinctive brass twist-lock knob
Mismatched ABS panel repairs—genuine Strata panels mixed with cheaper Shelf fabricator knockoffs, visibly different finishes
Carved or spray-painted personal identification marks—miner names, date marks, tally notches for shifts worked
Multiple cargo pockets with welded seams and reinforced stitching
Anchor points and D-rings along sides for carabiners and safety equipment
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 2 corpo manufacturing (Strata Deep Industrial) downgraded by Tier 4 knockoff repairs and field salvage. The suit signals working-class labor with access to corporate equipment, but the visible patch-work and paint marks indicate a miner—someone in the depths where status symbols don't matter.
physical_description.cultural_context: Wearing this suit means you work in pressurized subsurface zones—dangerous, unglamorous, well-compensated labor. The hand-painted marks are intimate; they're how you claim identity in darkness. The visible repairs indicate experience and survival: you've been down long enough to break things and fix them yourself. It's a badge of hard work, not fashion.
physical_description.condition_typical: Weathered and heavily used. The matte finish is dulled by dust and mineral deposits. ABS panels show spider-crack stress patterns; several are obviously non-original replacements (different plastic type, slightly different shade). The sealed face shield is often clouded from constant humidity and micro-scratches. Pressure seals are grimy. Paint marks are faded or layered from years of re-marking. The suit looks lived-in, abused, trusted.

image_prompt: A Tier 4 miner in a battle-worn Strata Deep TunnelHide pressure suit, standing in a moody industrial deep-mine facility. The suit is charcoal-gray cordura with mismatched black ABS polymer reinforcement panels—some original Strata-branded, some clearly cheap knockoff Shelf fab units with visible stress cracks. The integrated exoframe harness runs visibly along the spine. The sealed face shield reflects cool tungsten work-lights, slightly fogged and clouded. White spray-painted tally marks and a name run down the suit's side. Dust and mineral deposits coat the material. Harsh overhead lighting creates stark shadows on the reinforced panels. Dark concrete and jagged rock face backdrop. Moody, claustrophobic industrial atmosphere. --ar 2:3 --v 6
